(Search snippet content — full article 403'd on direct fetch; Times of Israel's own reporting language)
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud is trying to delay the certification of the official election results, as the party continues to push its claim that the vote was "stolen" by non-Zionist Arab parties. Likud lawyer and CEC member Ilan Bombach wrote to the committee's chair Justice Noam Sohlberg requesting an urgent meeting before the vote is certified, arguing that the seriousness of foreign interference suspicions and lack of clarity do not allow for publishing the certified results. Sohlberg rejected Bombach's request to put off certifying the results, writing that the Central Election Committee has no authority to withhold certification of the results or to intervene in an ongoing investigation. President Isaac Herzog will receive the official election results from the Central Elections Committee chairman Justice Noam Sohlberg on Wednesday and will begin consultations at the President's Residence.
